title: Newspaper Clippings & Report - Officer Cites Withdrawal Aids Defense

page_data.en:
THE CHINA PRESS, THURSDAY, MARCH 3, 1932
3368
D. 3325.
4 - 3 - 32

OFFICER CITES
WITHDRAWAL
AIDS DEFENSE

Japanese Advantage Said
Eliminated Through
Strategic Move

A high officer of the Chinese army has issued the following statement through the Kuo Min News Agency:

“Our army fighting around Shanghai has withdrawn in good order to the second line of defense. This move has been throughout a foregone conclusion, and it was only a question of time when it would have to be carried out. If ever there was a strategical retirement, this retirement is one, for in fighting in the first line of defense, the advantages are all with the Japanese.

“The original line occupied by the Chinese forces from Chapei to Woosung was not a military one and adopted only owing to the exigencies of the political situation, for it presents no possibility of an offensive as the Chinese army is loath to attack the International Settlement although it has been used as a base of operations by the Japanese.

“In the second place, the defense line is located behind the Whangpoo River, which is dominated by Japanese warships that are constantly keeping our line under fire from their heavy guns.

“Thirdly, the Chinese troops around Shanghai, although numerically are of about the same number as the Japanese, owing to the lack of transports could put in the field half the number of effectives.

Extensive Front

“As the resistance against Japan is a national one and as the Japanese navy completely controls the Yangtze and Whangpoo Rivers, our troops have to be scattered at all threatened points so the concentration of troops around the first line of defense would never be as large as the forces that Japan is capable of throwing into Shanghai.

“Fourthly, all the roads of the Settlement and the main motor road between Shanghai and Woosung are within rifle range of the Japanese warships and held by the Japanese tanks. With these roads to operate upon, the Japanese could easily bring up all their tanks, armored cars and heavy artillery, while the Chinese troops have to depend on narrow muddy paths to bring up supplies from the rear. With the Japanese army in command of the railways and river routes, the

Japanese had are completely reversed. The Japanese army would be operating away from the protection of their warships. It would have no roads where their tanks and heavy guns could be brought up and every step their soldiers take would be away from their base. On the other hand, for the Chinese army the rear is protected; their lines brings them to their own country, reinforcement could reach them easily, and all the advantages of the terrain will be with them.

No Surrender

“The public is asking what will be the next step. It is abundantly clear that the Government will never conclude any agreement with Japan derogative to the sovereign rights of the nation. If the Japanese army choose to attack our second line of defence, we would fight them; and if we are compelled again by superior numbers and equipment to retire, we will retire in order to fight them again. Far from ending, the fight is just beginning.

“For over a month our troops have been facing the might of Japan unafraid. The Japanese army has brought with them tanks, airplanes, field artillery and the latest howitzers—all the devices that human ingenuity could perfect. Our troops have had only rifles and machine guns to face the overwhelming mass of Japanese artillery, the supporting fire of naval guns, and Japanese airplanes spotting the range.

“As a foreign Military Attache said, the battlefield looked more like a sham battle than the stern reality of war, because all the artillery firing came from the Japanese as the Chinese guns have been put out of commission by the bombing and shelling of the planes and warships. The stout Chinese infantry could only remain in the trenches stoically receiving the barrage of Japanese artillery and bombs from the Japanese airplanes. It was only after the third engagement for the assault that the Chinese could return the shell and machine gun fire.

“The fighting around Shanghai has demonstrated beyond any doubt shows that the boasted invincibility of the Japanese army and navy is nothing but an empty myth. On the other hand, despite the overwhelming superiority of Japanese preparations, the whole world has been made aware of the indomitable spirit of the Chinese people.”

Y
3/3

《字林西报》，1932年3月3日，星期四
3368
D. 3325.
4 - 3 - 32

军官称
撤退
有助防御

据称日军优势
已通过战略行动
消除

中国军队一名高级军官通过国民新闻社发表如下声明：

“我军在上海周边作战的部队已有序撤至第二道防线。此举早已在预料之中，执行只是时间问题。若说这是战略性撤退，那便是，因为在第一道防线作战，优势全在日军一方。

“中国军队最初从闸北至吴淞所占据的防线并非军事防线，而是因政治局势紧迫而采取的权宜之计，因为该线不具备进攻可能；尽管日军将其作为行动基地，但中国军队不愿攻击公共租界。

“其次，这道防线位于黄浦江后方，而黄浦江受日本军舰控制，日舰不断以重炮轰击我方防线。

“第三，上海周边的中国军队虽然在人数上与日军大致相当，但由于缺乏运输工具，能投入战场的有效兵力仅有一半。

战线漫长

“由于抗日是全民性的抵抗，且日本海军完全控制长江和黄浦江，我军不得不分散部署在所有受威胁的地点，因此第一道防线周围的兵力集结永远无法达到日本能投入上海的兵力规模。

“第四，租界内的所有道路以及上海与吴淞之间的主要公路均处于日本军舰的步枪射程之内，并由日本坦克控制。凭借这些道路，日军可以轻松调动其所有坦克、装甲车和重型火炮，而中国军队则必须依靠狭窄泥泞的小路从后方运送补给。随着日军掌控铁路和水路，

局势完全逆转。日军将在远离其军舰保护的情况下作战。他们将没有道路可供坦克和重炮推进，士兵每前进一步都在远离其基地。另一方面，对中国军队而言，后方受到保护；他们的战线通向本国国土，增援可以轻易到达，地形的一切优势都将在我方。

绝不投降

“公众询问下一步将如何行动。显而易见，政府绝不会与日本达成任何损害国家主权的协议。如果日军选择攻击我们的第二道防线，我们将与之战斗；如果我们再次因敌军数量和装备优势而被迫撤退，我们将撤退以便再次与之战斗。战斗远未结束，才刚刚开始。

“一个多月来，我军无畏地面对日本的武力。日军带来了坦克、飞机、野战炮和最新式的榴弹炮——人类智慧所能完善的所有武器。而我军仅凭步枪和机枪，去应对压倒性的日军炮兵群、舰炮的支援火力以及为日军校正射击范围的日本飞机。

“正如一位外国武官所说，战场看起来更像是一场演习，而非战争的严峻现实，因为所有的炮火都来自日军，中国火炮已被飞机和军舰的轰炸与炮击摧毁。英勇的中国步兵只能坚守战壕，坚忍地承受日军炮兵和日本飞机投下的炸弹 barrage。直到第三次遭遇战后，中国军队才能以炮弹和机枪火力还击。

“上海周边的战斗毫无疑问地表明，日军吹嘘的海陆军无敌神话不过是空谈。另一方面，尽管日军准备具有压倒性优势，但全世界都已认识到中国人民不屈不挠的精神。”

Y
3/3

page_data.en:
THE CHINA PRESS, THURSDAY, MARCH 3, 1932.
3357

19th Route Army
Determined Not
Waver In Fight

Withdrawal Necessary But
Enemy Will Be Resisted
To Last Soldier

Determination to continue to
wage war against Japan from their
second line of defense, was set
forth in the circular telegram which
the 19th Route Army despatched to
the National Government and the
Central Kuomintang Headquarters
late last night.

The telegram states: "We have
been resisting Japanese invasion for
more than one month in spite of
the fact that our enemy is equipped with superior weapons and
enjoys better facilities for transportation.

"Encouraged by our people, we
have fought against Japanese invaders bravely, and in spite of our
heavy casualties we could still repulse them.

Suffer Losses

"All of a sudden, the Japanese
added two fresh divisions to their
fighting forces, but on account of
the difficulty of transportation we
were unable to ensure the continuous arrival of our reinforcements.
"Since February 21, our troops
daily suffered severe casualties, and
we have been obliged to put all of
our available forces on the main
fronts.

"At such a time, one Japanese
division landed at Liuho, and we
were unable to spare troops to meet
this flank attack. Consequently our
positions in the rear were endangered.

Steady Resistance

"In the circumstances we were
obliged to order all of our forces on
the evening of March 1 to withdraw
to their second line of defense.

3/3
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》，1932年3月3日，星期四。
3357

第十九路军
决心坚持抗战
不动摇

撤退虽有必要
但将抵抗至
最后一兵一卒

第十九路军于昨晚向国民政府和国民党中央总部发出的通电中，阐述了从第二道防线继续对日作战的决心。

电文称：“尽管敌人装备精良，拥有更优越的运输条件，但我军已抵抗日本入侵一个多月。

“在民众的鼓舞下，我们英勇抗击日本侵略者，尽管伤亡惨重，但仍能击退他们。

遭受损失

“突然，日军增加了两个师团加入战斗部队，但由于运输困难，我们无法确保增援部队持续抵达。
“自2月21日以来，我军每日遭受严重伤亡，我们不得不将所有可用兵力投入主要前线。

“在此时刻，一个日本师团在浏河登陆，我们无法抽调兵力应对这一侧翼攻击。因此，我后方阵地受到威胁。

坚定抵抗

“在此情况下，我们不得不下令所有部队于3月1日晚撤至第二道防线。

3/3

March 3, 1932.                                  Morning Translation

MILITARY

China Times

WITHDRAWAL OF CHINESE TROOPS.

        For strategetic purposes, the 19th Route Army
commenced the withdrawal from all fronts on the night of
March 1. This retreat is not the result of defeat and
was carried out in perfect order without any loss. The
Japanese did not occupy the lines evacuated by the
Chinese before they received the information. It is
reported that the Japanese vanguards reached Chenju last
night. The Chinese troops are now concentrating at a
certain place and have constructed new second defence
lines. In addition, the Chinese army is determined to
resist to the last.

Chinese Forces At Liuho Withdraw First.

        According to information received from military
sources, about 20,000 Japanese soldiers landed at Liuk
during the night. They immediately started to attack
the Chinese lines and serious fighting ensued. Continuous
Japanese reinforcements totally outnumbered the Chinese
who began to retreat.
        Following the evacuation of Liuho, the Chinese
troops at Tazang, Kiangwan, Miaohong and other places
also withdrew. The Japanese soldiers first occupied
Yangchiazah, then Chingchiamohdou and afterwards proceeded
to Tazang.
        At 11 a.m. yesterday 2,000 Japanese soldiers
arrived at Tazang from Kiangwan. Cavalry detachments
attacked the Chinese lines. The Chinese Big Sword Corps
engaged them with grenades etc. Fighting lasted till
3 p.m.
        The Radio Station at Chenju was occupied by
Japanese vanguards at 7 p.m. yesterday.

Eastern Times

WOOSUNG FORTS STILL IN CHINESE HANDS.

        Brigadier-General Ccn Tso Hoen and General Don
Chi Seu, Commandant of the Woosung Forts, who are prepared
to die for the Forts, refused to retreat with the others,
so consequently a number of soldiers are still remaining
in the Forts.
        About 7 a.m. yesterday, four Japanese aeroplanes
reconnoitred the Sz Ts Ling Forts preparatory to dropping
bombs. They flew away when Chinese anti-aircraft guns were
fired. At 2.30 p.m. five Japanese warships shelled the
Forts. The shells, however, all dropped in vacant fields.
At 3 p.m. the Forts replied and continued the cannonade
till 3.30 p.m. when the guns of both sides became
comparatively quiet. At 5 p.m. Japanese men-of-war again
opened fire on the Forts and both belligerent still
continue the engagement.

1932年3月3日。                                  晨间译稿

军事

《时报》

中国军队撤退。

        出于战略目的，第十九路军于3月1日晚开始从各前线撤退。此次撤退并非战败所致，而是秩序井然地进行，没有任何损失。日军在收到消息前并未占领中国军队撤离的阵地。据报道，日军先头部队昨晚抵达真如。中国军队目前正集中于某地，并已构筑新的第二道防线。此外，中国军队决心抵抗到底。

浏河中国军队首先撤退。

        据军方消息来源称，约2万名日军于夜间在浏河（Liuk）登陆。他们立即开始攻击中国军队阵地，随即爆发激烈战斗。日军增援部队源源不断，人数完全超过中国军队，后者开始撤退。
        继浏河撤离后，大场、江湾、庙行等地的中国军队也相继撤退。日军首先占领杨家宅，随后占领纪家桥，接着推进至大场。
        昨日上午11时，2000名日军从江湾抵达大场。骑兵分队攻击中国军队阵地。中国大刀队用手榴弹等武器与之交战。战斗持续至下午3时。
        昨晚7时，真如无线电台被日军先头部队占领。

《东方日报》

吴淞炮台仍在中国军队手中。

        吴淞炮台指挥官秦佐华准将和邓志修将军誓死保卫炮台，拒绝随其他部队撤退，因此仍有部分士兵留守炮台。
        昨日上午7时许，四架日本飞机侦察狮子林炮台，准备投弹。当中国高射炮开火后，它们飞离。下午2时30分，五艘日本军舰炮击炮台。然而，炮弹全部落在空旷田野中。下午3时，炮台还击，并持续炮击至下午3时30分，此时双方炮声相对平息。下午5时，日本军舰再次向炮台开火，交战双方仍在继续战斗。

March 3, 1932. Morning Translation

MISCELLANEOUS

China Times and other local newspapers

MR. YUI ONG KUIN'S STATEMENT.

In connection with the withdrawal of Chinese troops, Mr. Yui Ong Kuin, Chief Secretary of the Municipality of Greater Shanghai, yesterday made the following statement:-
"The withdrawal carried out by our army is a strategical one due to the fact that the Japanese reinforcements had been landed at Liuhc. This retreat is entirely political and is not because of any defect. Our withdrawal is a move which dovetails in war tactics with our general plan and we shall continue to resist until the last man. I hope the public will remain calm and will heartily support the government in its resistance of the common foe. The Municipality and its subordinate bureaux will continue to function as usual. The police force and the merchant volunteer corps, now remaining in Nantao, are sufficient to maintain peace and order. We already know that Japan is not sincere in her talk about the peace movement and now we can understand more fully her aims".

China Times and other local newspapers

MEETING OF LOCAL MERCHANTS AND CITIZENS.

At 3 p.m. yesterday, the Shanghai Special District Citizens Federation and the Federation of Street Unions held an urgent joint meeting which was attended by over 80 representatives and was presided over by Chang Ts Lien.
The following resolutions were passed:-
(1) That urgent notices be issued to members advising them to remain calm as the withdrawal of the 19th Route Army to Nanziang is simply a strategic move.
(2) That a telegram be sent to the Central Government petitioning it to dispatch reinforcements immediately to recover Woosung and Shanghai.
(3) That a manifesto be issued requesting the 19th Route Army to continue the war and promising the support of 3,000,000 local citizens.
(4) That representatives be appointed to question and dissuade the minority of shopkeepers who have resumed business.
(5) That representatives be detailed to request the Shanghai Chamber of Commerce to adopt a similar attitude towards our Federations and also to persuade the Since, Wing Ong and Sun Sun Companies to suspend business.

1932年3月3日。晨间译稿

杂项

《时报》及其他本地报纸

俞鸿钧先生声明。

    关于中国军队撤退一事，大上海市政府秘书长俞鸿钧先生昨日发表如下声明：
    “我军进行的撤退是战略性的，原因是日军已在浏河登陆。此次撤退完全是政治性的，并非因为任何缺陷。我们的撤退是与总体计划相契合的战争战术举措，我们将抵抗至最后一人。希望公众保持冷静，衷心支持政府抵抗共同敌人。市政府及其下属局处将继续照常运作。目前留在南市的警察力量和商团义勇队足以维持和平与秩序。我们已知日本在和谈运动中并无诚意，现在我们可以更充分地理解其目标”。

《时报》及其他本地报纸

本地商民会议。

    昨日下午3时，上海特别区市民联合会和各马路商界联合会举行紧急联席会议，出席代表80余人，由张慈连主持。
    通过以下决议：
    (1) 向会员发布紧急通知，劝告他们保持冷静，因为第十九路军撤至南翔仅是战略举措。
    (2) 致电中央政府，请求立即派遣增援部队收复吴淞和上海。
    (3) 发表宣言，请求第十九路军继续抗战，并承诺300万本地市民的支持。
    (4) 指派代表质问并劝阻少数已复业的店主。
    (5) 指派代表请求上海总商会对我各联合会采取类似态度，并劝说新昌、永安和先施公司停业。

page_data.en:
March 3, 1932. Morning Translation.

MISCELLANEOUS.

Shun Pao:-

NANKING FOREIGN OFFICE ISSUES MANIFESTO.

The Nanking Ministry of Foreign
Affairs issued the following manifesto on March 2:-
"Owing to the Japanese having again
launched their general attack on Liuhо and Woosung
since being reinforced by two divisions, we have to
make the following announcement:-
"Through the endeavours and mediation
of Admiral Kelley of the British Navy, representatives
of China and Japan were invited to attend a conference
the object of which was to bring about the immediate
cessation of the Sino-Japanese military activities.
The following conditions were proposed to both belligerents:-
1. Both sides to withdraw simultaneously.
2. The plan to demolish permanently the Woosung
and Lion Wood Forts should not be proposed.
3. The withdrawal by both sides of their forces
to be supervised by a Sino-Japanese Committee
together with representatives of neutral countries.
4. The evacuated districts to be governed by
Chinese officials and to be policed by Chinese
as formerly.
5. The Chinese troops withdraw to Chenju and the
Japanese troops to withdraw into the International
Settlement, the former to withdraw to Nanziang
and the Japanese forces to be embarked in
their battleships.
"The fifth clause to be discussed
further at the next conference.
"Should the above terms for a reconcilia-
tion be actually agreed to by both the Japanese and
Chinese Governments, then a formal conference will be
held by diplomatic and military representatives of both
sides.
"On February 29, the Chinese
representatives informed Admiral Kelley that the Chinese
Government agreed to the above terms for the cessation
of hostilities and requested Admiral Kelley to transmit
this decision to the Japanese Government and in the
event of the Japanese Government coinciding, a formal
conference should be immediately convoked. The Tokyo
Government failed to offer any answer for several days
during which time the Japanese military, aerial and
naval forces continued to launch their "big push",
and simultaneously, the Japanese Consul-General
informed our Mayor that the Japanese forces had determined
to destroy the Shanghai-Nanking and Shanghai-Hangchow
Railways. As China has continuously strove for peace,
the responsibility for the further breach of the Peace
Conference rests with Japan".
page_data.zh:
1932年3月3日。晨间译件。

杂项。

《申报》：

南京外交部发表宣言。

南京外交部于3月2日发表如下宣言：
“鉴于日军在增援两个师团后，再次对浏河和吴淞发动全面进攻，我方不得不发表如下声明：
“经英国海军凯利（Kelley）上将的努力与调停，中日双方代表受邀参加会议，旨在促使中日军事行动立即停止。向交战双方提出了以下条件：
1. 双方同时撤军。
2. 不应提出永久拆除吴淞及狮子林炮台的计划。
3. 双方撤军应由一个中日委员会会同中立国代表进行监督。
4. 撤离地区由中国官员治理，并由中国人像以往一样维持治安。
5. 中国军队撤至真如，日本军队撤入公共租界；前者撤至南翔，日本部队则登舰。
“第五款将在下次会议上进一步讨论。
“如果上述和解条款确实得到日本和中国政府的同意，那么双方外交和军事代表将举行正式会议。
“2月29日，中方代表告知凯利上将，中国政府同意上述停战条款，并请凯利上将将此决定转达日本政府；若日本政府同意，应立即召开正式会议。东京政府数日未作答复，在此期间，日本陆、空、海军继续发动‘大攻势’，同时，日本总领事通知我方市长，日军已决定摧毁沪宁铁路和沪杭铁路。鉴于中国一直致力于和平，破坏和谈的责任在于日本。”

page_data.en:
March 3, 1932.
Morning Translation.

MISCELLANEOUS

Sin Wan Pao and other local newspapers :

GOVERNMENT LEADERS ACCUSED OF BETRAYING THE NATION.

Mr. Sun Fo and Mr. Eugene Chen, members of
the Central Executive Committee of the National Government,
made the following joint statement to our reporter :-
"The real cause for the general withdrawal of
the 19th Route Army is due to lack of reinforcements.
It will be remembered that the higher military authorities
of the 19th Route Army sent an urgent telegram to the
Government several weeks ago demanding the immediate dispatch
of reinforcements to consolidate the Chinese defensive lines
at Liuhо and vicinity. General Chiang Kai-shek in a
telegraphic reply to the 19th Route Army stated that
reinforcements would arrive at the above mentioned places
within a week. We were almost reduced to tears because
no reinforcements arrived. The above is no fabrication
as General Chen Ming-shu vouched for it himself when he
visited us at our residence. At such a time and in such
circumstances when we are outnumbered, we can only suffer
in silence. In view of this, what the Government promised
in the form of concrete measures to resist Japan is simply
a falsehood imposed upon the masses. It is absolutely
preposterous that at the most critical moment which might
possibly mean the ruination of China, they (the Government
leaders) have acted against their conscience at the present
time. Those who have betrayed the nation must be
definitely made public."

Sin Wan Pao and other local newspapers :

19TH ROUTE ARMY DETERMINED NEVER TO WAVER.

Yesterday, Generals Chiang Kwan Nai, Tsai Ding
Kai and Tai Chi, Commanders of the Chinese troops who have
have been fighting the Japanese since January 28, dispatched
a joint circular telegram the full text of which appears
in the China Press to-day.

Sin Wan Pao and other local newspapers :

MILITARY STATEMENT BY CHINESE OFFICER EXPLAINING WITHDRAWAL
OF CHINESE ARMY.

The full text of this statement also appears
in the China Press to-day.

1932年3月3日。
晨间译件。

杂项

《新闻报》及其他本地报纸：

政府领袖被指控卖国。

国民政府中央执行委员会委员孙科先生和陈友仁（Eugene Chen）先生向记者发表联合声明如下：
“第十九路军全面撤退的真正原因是缺乏增援。记得几周前，第十九路军高级军事当局曾向政府发出急电，要求立即派遣增援部队以巩固浏河及附近地区的中国防线。蒋介石将军在回复第十九路军的电报中表示，增援部队将在一周内抵达上述地点。我们几乎痛哭流涕，因为没有任何增援到达。以上并非捏造，陈铭枢将军在访问我们寓所时亲自为此作证。在这种敌众我寡的时刻和情况下，我们只能默默忍受。有鉴于此，政府承诺的抵抗日本的具体措施简直是对民众施加的谎言。在最关键的时刻——这可能意味着中国的毁灭——他们（政府领袖）目前违背良心的行为是绝对荒谬的。那些卖国贼必须公之于众。”

《新闻报》及其他本地报纸：

第十九路军决心毫不动摇。

昨日，自1月28日以来一直与日军作战的中国军队指挥官蒋光鼐、蔡廷锴和戴戟将军发出联名通电，全文刊登于今日的《字林西报》。

《新闻报》及其他本地报纸：

中国军官就中国军队撤退发表的军事声明。

该声明全文亦刊登于今日的《字林西报》。

page_data.en:
March 3, 1932. Afternoon Translation.

MILITARY
Eastern Times:

JAPANESE MOVEMENTS AFTER CHINESE EVACUATION.

Chinese troops stationed in Nantao and along the Shanghai-Hangchow Railway Line have been withdrawn to Too Jao Sin Tsong. As for the Garrison Commissioner's Headquarters, these were not removed to the above place from Lunghwa until 10 a.m. yesterday when the whole line withdrew and the defense work at the rear was finished. Great numbers of Chinese soldiers are still stationed in Lungchow, forming the first line of defense along Shanghai-Hangchow Line.

At first, the Japanese soldiers dared not proceed far into Chapei, after the Chinese troops had withdrawn. At 10 a.m. Japanese plainclothes men began to proceed forward from Jukong Road in the direction of North Station. At Tientungan, Japanese plainclothes men preceded the infantry who were protected by heavy artillery. They proceeded slowly from Hwang Pang Jao in a south-westerly direction and reached Soong Kung Yuan Road at 5.30 p.m. After the Japanese vanguard had reached Chapei, the Japanese in Yangtszepoo district also arrived at Paoshan Road via Broadway, Hongkew Market and North Szechuen Road. Some six tanks preceded the vanguard, whose rear was brought up by machine guns, light guns, and artillery. It took them two hours, i.e. from 3.30 to 5.30 p.m., to reach Chapei.

At 3.30 p.m. yesterday after the Chinese had evacuated, the Japanese began to proceed westward in the direction of the Woosung-Shanghai Railway Line. They fired machine guns, rifles and light guns en route. At 4 p.m. seven men of the above party arrived at North Station. They entered the Station and made a search, after which they went up to second floor from which place they conducted observations in all directions. A number of marines were stationed at Jukong, Paoshan, Paoshing Roads along the Woosung-Shanghai Railway Line. From the North Station westward to Markham Road, there were Japanese sentinels. The main body of the Japanese soldiers is still in Pah Sz Jao and Hongkew

JAPANESE AERIAL EXPLOITS.

The Eastern Times publishes the following telegrams from Soochow:-
At 8 a.m. March 2, six Japanese aeroplanes in an attempt to destroy the Tsing Yang railway bridge, dropped bombs in Chiang Ka Garden. At 11.30a.m. another nine aeroplanes appeared over the Tsing Yang railway bridge dropped twelve bombs, destroying it as also a part of the Railway Station.

At 10 a.m. March 2, twelve Japanese aeroplanes destroyed the Tai Chong School and Sin Hsa Bridge at Liuho.
page_data.zh:
1932年3月3日。午后译件。

军事
《时事新报》：

中国军队撤离后的日军动向。

驻守南市及沿沪杭铁路线的中国军队已撤至陶家辛庄（Too Jao Sin Tsong）。至于卫戍司令部，直到昨日上午10时全线撤退且后方防御工作完成后，才从龙华迁往上述地点。大量中国士兵仍驻扎在龙漕（Lungchow），构成沿沪杭线的第一道防线。

起初，在中国军队撤离后，日本士兵不敢深入闸北。上午10时，日本便衣人员开始从交通路向北站方向推进。在天通庵，日本便衣人员走在步兵前面，步兵由重炮掩护。他们从黄潘桥（Hwang Pang Jao）缓慢向西南方向推进，于下午5时30分到达宋公园路（Soong Kung Yuan Road）。日军先头部队到达闸北后，杨树浦区的日军也经由百老汇路、虹口市场和北四川路到达宝山路。约六辆坦克在先头部队之前，其后由机枪、轻炮和火炮跟进。他们花了两个小时，即从下午3时30分到5时30分，才到达闸北。

昨日午后3时30分，在中国人撤离后，日军开始沿沪宁铁路线向西推进。途中发射机枪、步枪和轻炮。下午4时，上述队伍中的七人到达北站。他们进入车站进行搜索，随后上到二楼，从那里向各个方向进行观察。一批海军陆战队士兵驻扎在沿沪宁铁路线的交通路、宝山路和宝兴路。从北站向西到麦根路（Markham Road），均有日本哨兵。日军主力仍在八字桥（Pah Sz Jao）和虹口。

日军空中战绩。

《时事新报》刊登了来自苏州的以下电报：
3月2日上午8时，六架日本飞机试图摧毁青阳铁路桥，在蒋家花园投下炸弹。上午11时30分，另有九架飞机出现在青阳铁路桥上空，投下十二枚炸弹，摧毁了桥梁以及部分火车站。

3月2日上午10时，十二架日本飞机摧毁了浏河的太冲学校和新华桥（Sin Hsa Bridge）。

page_data.en:
March 3, 1932. Afternoon Translation.

MILITARY.

According information supplied by a certain person who came to Shanghai from Kading by way of Nanziang, no Japanese soldiers were in Liuho in the forenoon of March 2 but some were landed at Yang Ling Kur. When he left Kading, eight Japanese aeroplanes were aimlessly dropping bombs in Kading. The residents there were all running in a westerly direction into the interior of the country for safety. It was about 1 p.m. when he reached Nanziang on foot and saw nine Japanese aeroplanes dropping bombs in the Nanziang Village. Numerous houses caught fire and refugees were seen streaming along the roads. He reached Shanghai at 6 p.m.

At 3.35 p.m. yesterday, a Japanese aeroplane appeared over Cho Ka Jao, Pe Ya Sz Road. It flew very low and when the pilot observed some ricksha coolies resting on the roadway, he fired at them with his machine guns. The coolies immediately ran away. A Komponese pedestrian was killed.

According to a reliable military report, two noiseless aeroplanes were unloaded at 8 a.m. yesterday, by Chinese labourers, from the s.s. "Dairen Maru" which is anchored at the Wayside Wharf. These aeroplanes were sent to the front in motor trucks.

Shun Pao:

JAPANESE OCCUPY CHINESE POSITIONS.

The Chinese troops retreated into the interior along the Nanking-Shanghai and Shanghai-Hangchow Railways early yesterday morning. The Japanese did not dare proceed before 5 p.m. after their two aeroplanes had reconnoitered the districts that were being evacuated. High Chinese military officers declared that any further advance on the new Chinese lines will be stoutly defended.

The Garrison Commissioners Headquarters have now removed to a certain place and the Municipality of Greater Shanghai will also be removed.

Following the Chinese retreat, the Japanese proceeded to Peisinching at 2 p.m. yesterday firing all the way. Chinese refugees were either killed by Japanese plainclothesmen or burnt to death in the wide-spread conflagration. The Japanese advanced as far as the village of Kiangchao, some three li from Peisinching.

ALL QUIET IN NANTAO.

Pandemonium reigned throughout the Nantao district after the Chinese retreated. Policemen patrolled the district as usual searching pedestrians. According to a declaration made by the Bureau of Public Safety, the Police main force in Nantao is sufficient to maintain the peace and order in that district.
page_data.zh:
1932年3月3日。午后译件。

军事。

据一位经南翔从嘉定来到上海的人士提供的消息，3月2日上午浏河没有日本士兵，但有一些人在杨林口（Yang Ling Kur）登陆。当他离开嘉定时，八架日本飞机正在嘉定漫无目的地投掷炸弹。那里的居民都向西逃往内地以求安全。他步行到达南翔时大约是下午1点，看到九架日本飞机在南翔村投掷炸弹。许多房屋起火，可以看到难民沿着道路涌流。他于下午6点到达上海。

昨天下午3时35分，一架日本飞机出现在曹家渡（Cho Ka Jao）贝勒路（Pe Ya Sz Road）上空。它飞得很低，当飞行员看到一些人力车夫在路面上休息时，他用机枪向他们射击。车夫们立即跑开。一名韩国行人被杀。

据一份可靠的军事报告称，昨天上午8时，中国劳工从停靠在韦赛德码头（Wayside Wharf）的“大连丸”号轮船上卸下了两架无声飞机。这些飞机由卡车运往前线。

《申报》：

日军占领中国阵地。

昨天清晨，中国军队沿京沪铁路和沪杭铁路向内地撤退。在两架飞机侦察了正在撤离的地区后，日军直到下午5时前都不敢前进。中国高级军官宣称，任何对新防线的进一步进犯都将遭到顽强抵抗。

卫戍司令部现已迁往某地，大上海市政府也将迁移。

随着中国军队的撤退，日军于昨天下午2时向裴家桥（Peisinching）推进，一路开火。中国难民要么被日本便衣人员杀害，要么在大火中被烧死。日军推进至距裴家桥约三里的江桥村（Kiangchao）。

南市一切平静。

中国军队撤退后，南市全区陷入混乱。警察像往常一样在该区巡逻，搜查行人。据公安局声明，南市的主要警力足以维持该区的和平与秩序。

page_data.en:
March 3, 1932. Afternoon Translation..

MISCELLANEOUS.

Shun Pao:
THE QUESTION ON CESSATION OF SHANGHAI WAR.

With regard to the cessation of the
Sino-Japanese hostilities in Shanghai, the Japanese replied
yesterday to the Chinese authorities. As the reply differs
somewhat from the real essence of the five points discussed
by Admiral Nomura, the Japanese Naval Commander and Dr.
Wellington Koo, the Chinese representative, on the flagship
Kent of the British Navy, the Chinese representatives should
apply to their Government for instruction. The diplomatic
Committee held its second conference in the residence of
Mr. T.V. Soong and was attended by Mr. T.V. Soong, the Minister
of Foreign Affairs, Kuo Tai Chi, the Vice Minister of
Foreign Affairs, H.H. Kung, Committee member of the Central
Government, General Wu Te-cheng, Mayor of the Shanghai
Municipality and Dr. Wellington Koo, Committee member of
Foreign Office. The discussion dealt with measures to
cope with the present situation.
Mr. Kuo Tai Chi called on the
British Ambassador to China at 3 p.m. and the American
Minister at 5 p.m. yesterday to exchange views on the present
situation, but no concrete measures were reached. He attended
the meeting held at 9 a.m. in the British Consulate at
which the British Ambassador and Admiral Kelly of the
British Navy were present.
Mr. Kuo Tai Chi proceeded then with
Dr. Wellington Koo to hold another conference in the
residence of T.V. Soong. This meeting broke up at
midnight. The decisions reached at the conference held
in Mr. T.V. Soong's house have been submitted to the
Government for consideration. It is stated that China
will insist on the settlement of Sino-Japanese conflict
and will treat the Shanghai embroglio and Manchurian
incident as one question. China will still refer to the
League of Nations for a decision of the whole question.

Sin Wen Pao and other local newspapers :

JAPANESE BRUTALITIES.

These Chinese soldiers at Chapei, who were
wounded in the engagement on the night of March 1 and who
were beyond reach yesterday of being transferred to the rear
for medical treatment, were either brutally slaughtered
or unmercifully thrown into the fire by the Japanese on
these latters' occupation of the evacuated front. Refugees
who had fled into the Settlement area from Chapei stated
yesterday that they witnessed Japanese soldiers in groups
of three and fives forcing the Kempcnese to direct them to
conduct a search of every house in the various districts of
Chapei. They further stated that the Japanese, on seeing
Chinese young females, first raped them, then murdered them
and lastly set fire on their houses. Great numbers of
old Chinese women and young children were thrown into the
fire while the Japanese looked on and listened to their
agonizing screams and painful cries of the Chinese with
delight. Two Chinese wounded soldiers whose legs and
hands had been rendered useless by the bombardment were

1932年3月3日。下午译件。

杂项。

《申报》：
关于上海战事停止的问题。

关于上海中日敌对行动的停止，日本方面昨日向中国当局作出答复。由于该答复与野村海军大将（日本海军司令）与中国代表顾维钧博士在英国海军“肯特”号旗舰上讨论的五点实质内容略有出入，中国代表应向本国政府请示指示。外交委员会在宋子文先生寓所举行第二次会议，出席者有外交部长宋子文先生、外交部次长郭泰祺、中央政府委员孔祥熙、上海市市长吴铁城将军以及外交部委员顾维钧博士。讨论涉及应对当前局势的措施。
郭泰祺先生于昨日下午3时拜访英国驻华大使，并于下午5时拜访美国公使，就当前局势交换意见，但未达成具体措施。他参加了上午9时在英国领事馆举行的会议，英国大使和英国海军凯利上将出席了该会议。
随后，郭泰祺先生与顾维钧博士前往宋子文寓所举行另一次会议。此次会议直至午夜才结束。在宋子文先生寓所举行的会议上达成的决定已提交政府审议。据悉，中国将坚持解决中日冲突，并将上海纠纷与满洲事变视为一个问题。中国仍将把整个问题提交国际联盟裁决。

《新闻报》及其他本地报纸：

日军的暴行。

那些在3月1日晚间的战斗中受伤、且昨日无法后送接受医疗救治的闸北中国士兵，在日军占领撤离的前线阵地后，要么被残忍屠杀，要么被无情地投入火中。昨日从闸北逃入租界地区的难民称，他们目睹日军三五一伙，强迫“康邦尼斯”（音译，指朝鲜人/台籍辅助人员等）带路，对闸北各区的每一户房屋进行搜查。他们还称，日军见到中国年轻女子，先实施强奸，随后将其杀害，最后纵火焚烧其房屋。大量中国老妇和幼童被投入火中，而日军则在一旁观看，带着快感聆听中国人痛苦的尖叫和哀嚎。两名因炮击导致手脚残废的中国伤兵被

March 3, 1932. Afternoon Translation.

MISCELLANEOUS

captured by Japanese soldiers who cut off their hands and
then ripped open their abdomen. Upon being informed of
this, the French missionaries and nuns offered up a prayer.
Many Chinese missionaries now request the foreign
missionaries for the sake of humanity to organise a relief
corps to relieve Chinese wounded soldiers and civilians who
still remain on the evacuated war zone of Chapei.

Sin Wan Pao and other local newspapers :

KOMPONESE START LOOTING IN EVACUATED AREA.

Yesterday at 3 p.m. before the Japanese soldiers
had entered the areas evacuated by the Chinese in Chapei,
a large number of Komponse were seen busy along the Chapei
areas digging into doors of the evacuated civilian houses
to commit theft.

China Times

EXECUTION OF A CHINESE TRAITOR.

At 1 p.m. yesterday, the Public Safety Bureau of
the Municipality of Greater Shanghai executed a Chinese
traitor named Dong Yoong Sun at the Chen Chi Mei Memorial
Tower, West Gate, who was employed by the Japanese.

The "Crystal", a three-day mosquito paper

MAIN CAUSE FOR THE GENERAL WITHDRAWAL OF CHINESE TROOPS.

In resisting the Japanese onslaught since
January 28, our soldiers have repeatedly scored victories
necessitating the change of four Japanese commanding officers
and the dispatch of 3 Divisions as reinforcements.
Notwithstanding their attacks, sectors along Woosung, Liaohong,
Kiangwan and Chapei were held by Chinese. It happened that
a certain military officer was arrested by Japanese and a
military map was found in his portfolio. This map gave full
details explaining the important strategetic positions of our
army and thus the whole secret of our military campaign was
revealed to the Japanese. On the night of February 29, the
Japanese, in full strength, attacked the Chinese rear defence
line at Liuhc and as a result the whole of the 14th Division
of Japanese soldiers was landed there, compelling our troops
to withdraw from all positions. The order for retreat was
given at 4 p.m. March 1 and it was completed at 5 a.m.
March 2. Prior to this order, fighting still continued
on all fronts.
The seizure of the military map referred to above
accounts for the loss of Woosung and Chapei.

1932年3月3日。下午译件。

杂项

日军俘虏，日军砍断他们的手，随后剖开他们的腹部。获悉此事后，法国传教士和修女进行了祈祷。许多中国传教士现在请求外国传教士出于人道主义组织救援队，以救助仍留在闸北撤离战区的中国伤兵和平民。

《新晚报》及其他本地报纸：

“康邦尼斯”（音译）在撤离区开始抢劫。

昨日下午3时，在日军进入闸北中国军队撤离的区域之前，有人看到大量“康邦尼斯”（音译）在闸北地区忙碌，撬开撤离平民房屋的门户进行盗窃。

《时报》

处决一名汉奸。

昨日下午1时，大上海市公安局在西城门陈其美纪念塔处决了一名受雇于日本的名为董永顺（音译）的中国汉奸。

三日刊小报《水晶》

中国军队全面撤退的主要原因。

自1月28日以来抵抗日军进攻期间，我军屡获胜利，致使日军四次更换指挥官，并派遣三个师团作为增援。尽管日军发动攻击，吴淞、浏河、江湾和闸北沿线的阵地仍由中国军队坚守。然而，一名军官被日军逮捕，其公文包中发现了一份军事地图。该地图详细解释了我军的重要战略位置，从而使我方整个战役的秘密暴露给日军。2月29日晚，日军全力攻击浏河（原文拼写为Liuhc，疑为Liuhe之误）的中国后方防线，结果日军第十四师团全部在此登陆，迫使我军从所有阵地撤退。撤退命令于3月1日下午4时下达，并于3月2日凌晨5时完成。在此命令之前，各战线战斗仍在继续。
上述军事地图的被缴获，导致了吴淞和闸北的失守。
